If you’re a member of The Fountain of Life Church and you were at yesterday’s service, we’re a little jealous. What do you mean you got to witness Pastor Jimmy Odukoya introduce his wife, Mo Jasmine Daniel, to the congregation in person?

Yes, right there at the church’s headquarters in Ilupeju, Lagos, the senior pastor had a special person to introduce, and he made sure everyone knew exactly who she was. As she joined him at the altar, he introduced her as Pastor Mo Odukoya, the church’s new first lady, and the congregation welcomed the couple with cheers and applause.

Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and his wife, Mo Jasmine Daniel, holding hands during their official introduction at The Fountain of Life Church

But before that introduction, Pastor Jimmy had a little story to tell. He spoke about how he had been navigating life alone since becoming the church’s senior pastor, and how he had been searching for someone to share the journey with. He invited Mo to join him, and the two walked up to the altar together, marking the moment with a warm reception from the congregation.

Pastor Jimmy Odukoya introduces his wife, Mo Jasmine Daniel, on stage at The Fountain of Life Church in Ilupeju, Lagos

For those who know Pastor Jimmy beyond the pulpit, there’s quite a bit to his story. He took over as senior pastor of The Fountain of Life Church in 2023, following the passing of his father, the late Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, who co-founded the ministry with his wife, Pastor Bimbo Odukoya. He is also an actor and musician, and film audiences may recognise him as Oba Ade in the 2022 historical film The Woman King, where he starred alongside Viola Davis.

Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and Mo Jasmine Daniel after announcing their marriage to the congregation

And now, there’s a new chapter to this story with Mo. Introduced to the congregation as Pastor Mo Odukoya, she is the daughter of Reverend Theophilus and Bolaji Daniel. She also took a moment to address the church, expressing her pleasure and honour at joining the ministry family.

item.content:encoded:
Christmas is now around the corner, and many of us will already be discussing plans for 2027. Some people will be thinking about new jobs, planning weddings or promising themselves they will finally start exercising next year.

Then there are the 1977 and 1987 babies for whom 2027 won’t simply be another year. It is the year they turn fifty or forty, a major milestone in the journey of life that gets everyone asking: “So, what are we doing?” As someone born in 1988, I may not be under pressure to make a similar decision for 2027, but I am close enough to know that my turn is approaching very quickly. And truth be told, the closer I get to forty, the less interested I become in throwing a large party simply because that is what people expect.

But after years of travelling, I have also realised that some of the most memorable celebrations are not necessarily the biggest. They are the ones connected to experiences. Like having a private villa breakfast which everyone will always talk about. The boat trip that almost ended with somebody losing their phone in the ocean. The birthday dinner beneath the stars. The destination everyone initially complained was too far, then refused to leave when the trip ended.

That is what makes a destination party special. It does not give you one evening. It gives you several days of memories.

So, if I were born in 1977 or 1987 and planning a milestone birthday for 2027, I would spend my birthday seeing the world, and these are the destination celebrations I would surely consider, even better if you’re celebrating with your friends:

Bali, Indonesia

You know that friendship group that has been saying, “Girls’ trip soon,” for the past five years? Every January, somebody opens the conversation again. Everyone agrees. Dates are suggested, then work happens, children happen, school fees happen, someone suddenly has a wedding; something always comes up and halts every plan. Before you know it, another year has passed.

A fortieth or fiftieth birthday may finally be the excuse everyone needs, and Bali works beautifully because you can create a luxurious group experience without forcing everyone into separate hotel rooms.

Imagine ten friends sharing a private villa with a swimming pool and staff. Begin with a welcome dinner. Add a spa morning, beach club, waterfalls, rice terraces and, on the birthday itself, a private chef and dinner beneath the stars.

The greatest advantage of Bali is that luxury can still feel attainable. Just remember that Bali is not the place to invite people who cannot sit still. Some days, the entire plan may simply be breakfast, massage, swimming and sunset. And that is the itinerary. Private villa, poolside dinner, spa morning and sunset beach club–the perfect birthday idea.

Thailand

Thailand is for the celebrant who wants everything: City energy, beautiful beaches, nightlife, shopping, culture and food. It gives you enough value for money to stop your guests from sending angry voice notes about the budget.

Begin in Bangkok. Give everyone time to arrive and recover. Host a rooftop welcome dinner overlooking the city. Then fly to Phuket or Krabi. Book a villa or resort close to the beach. Arrange a private yacht or traditional long-tail boat. Add island hopping and a birthday dinner by the sea.

The birthday idea: Bangkok rooftop welcome, Phuket villa stay, private boat celebration and beach dinner.

Mexico

If you want a birthday everyone will still be talking about five years later, Mexico is for you. Cancún gives you all-inclusive resorts, beach clubs and nightlife. Tulum offers beautiful villas, restaurants and cenotes. Cabo brings dramatic coastline, polished resorts and excellent settings for sunset dinners and boat parties.

For a milestone birthday, choose one base rather than trying to cover the entire country. Have a relaxed welcome evening. Settle in. Centre the birthday around a private catamaran followed by dinner on the beach.

Then leave one day completely free. Trust me. A destination birthday should not feel like military service. The birthday idea: All-inclusive resort, catamaran celebration, beach dinner and one recovery day.

Morocco

There are birthday parties, then there are birthday scenes. Morocco gives you scenes.

Picture everyone arriving at a beautiful riad in Marrakech. Lanterns glowing in the courtyard. Mint tea on arrival. Everyone admiring the architecture before immediately asking for the WiFi password. Spend a day exploring the souks or book a hammam experience. For the birthday itself, leave the city. Imagine a private desert dinner with music, candles and the Atlas Mountains in the background. Morocco already gives you colour, texture, food and atmosphere. You do not need to overproduce it. The birthday idea: Marrakech riad takeover, rooftop welcome dinner, hammam and private desert celebration.

Jamaica

Jamaica will always be personal for me. It is one of those places where celebration feels natural. Music is not added at the end. It is already part of the experience. It gives you a birthday that celebrates life, not just age.

Rent a villa overlooking the Caribbean Sea. Arrange a jerk barbecue outside. Add a live reggae band or DJ. Spend one day on a catamaran and another exploring waterfalls. Then spend another doing absolutely nothing except eating, talking and enjoying the view. After forty or fifty years of life, perhaps that is exactly the point. The birthday idea: Private villa, Jamaican barbecue, live music, catamaran and waterfall excursion.

Jordan

Not every milestone birthday needs beach clubs and loud music; some deserve wonder. Imagine your group walking through the narrow Siq before Petra suddenly appears. Spend time floating in the Dead Sea. Book a night in Wadi Rum. Arrange a private desert dinner beneath the stars. Jordan works particularly well for smaller groups because the experience feels personal. Ten people is ideal, large enough to create energy and small enough to move comfortably. The birthday idea: Petra, Dead Sea relaxation and a private Wadi Rum desert dinner.

Brazil

Some destinations are beautiful; Brazil feels alive. Base yourself in Rio. Get an easy first evening of dinner, drinks and music. Then move between the beach, Sugarloaf Mountain, Christ the Redeemer, rooftop dinners and samba nights.

For the birthday, arrange a private boat day followed by dinner with live Brazilian music. If you want deeper cultural connections, you can include Salvador for Afro-Brazilian heritage, food and music. Brazil will not reduce its energy simply because the celebrant is now forty or fifty. The birthday idea: Rio beach stay, private boat party, white dinner and live samba.

Marbella, Spain

If you have been paying attention to Nigerian destination celebrations recently, you may have noticed Marbella appearing more frequently. I understand why. In the last few months alone, Marbella has provided the backdrop for major Nigerian family celebrations and destination weddings.

More recently, my team also worked with clients who chose Marbella for a 35th birthday celebration, bringing together a group of 20 people. For me, that was useful because Marbella moved from somewhere I could recommend in theory to somewhere I have now seen work for a Nigerian celebration group in practice.

Marbella gives you many of the things Nigerians already love. Beautiful hotels and villas. Beach clubs, yachts, restaurants, nightlife, and sunshine.

For a fortieth or fiftieth, I would give everyone an arrival day, have a proper welcome dinner, choose one or two major group experiences and leave enough space for people to enjoy Spain. Our recent group taught us something important: You do not need to programme every hour.

Twenty adults will not necessarily want to wake up, eat, swim, shop and party at the same time. The bigger consideration for Nigerians planning Marbella in 2027 is the visa. Spain is within the Schengen Area, so Nigerian passport holders who require visas need to factor applications and appointments into the planning timeline.

When one person travels, their visa is their responsibility. When you are trying to move twenty people for a birthday, visas become part of event planning. Marbella is a destination to start planning well in advance. Know who genuinely intends to travel. Identify who already has valid visas and who needs to apply. Set payment deadlines. Get accommodation arrangements organised early.

The glamorous part may be the birthday dinner overlooking the Mediterranean. The successful part is having everyone who was supposed to be in the photograph actually make it to Spain. The birthday idea: Málaga arrival, Marbella hotel or villa stay, welcome dinner, beach club or yacht day and Mediterranean birthday dinner.

Albania and Montenegro

If people have travelled all the way to Europe for your birthday, why not give them two countries? Begin in Tirana before moving towards the Albanian Riviera. Sarandë and Ksamil offer blue water, seafood restaurants, villas and boat experiences without necessarily carrying the prices of Mykonos or the South of France.

Then continue by road into Montenegro. The scenery changes completely. Budva gives you beaches and nightlife. Kotor offers history and dramatic views. Tivat and Porto Montenegro provide a polished setting for the final dinner.

Two countries, two moods and one milestone birthday. Just confirm entry requirements for every traveller before collecting money. Residency permits, existing visas and nationality can affect entry conditions. The birthday idea: Tirana welcome dinner, Albanian Riviera villa, road journey into Montenegro, yacht day and waterfront dinner.

Qatar

Qatar works for the celebrant who wants elegance without unnecessary chaos. It is also useful when guests are travelling from different parts of the world because Doha is a major international hub. Spend time exploring Souq Waqif. Arrange a desert dinner. Book a yacht. Choose one of Doha’s luxury hotels for the birthday evening.

The celebration could end there, or Qatar could become the opening chapter before the group continues to Thailand, Bali or another Asian destination. It can be the entire birthday or a warm-up. The birthday idea: Luxury hotel stay, desert celebration, yacht experience and elegant dinner.

Elizabeth’s Milestone Birthday Budget Guide

These are indicative planning estimates for groups sharing rooms or villas, staying approximately four to seven nights, with local transport, a main celebration and selected activities. They exclude international flights, visa fees, personal shopping and individual spending.

Destination Suggested Stay Estimated Cost Per Person Group of 10
Bali 5 to 6 nights $1,100 to $1,700 $11,000 to $17,000
Thailand 6 nights $1,200 to $1,900 $12,000 to $19,000
Mexico 5 nights $1,500 to $2,400 $15,000 to $24,000
Morocco 5 nights $1,200 to $1,900 $12,000 to $19,000
Jamaica 5 to 6 nights $1,700 to $2,800 $17,000 to $28,000
Jordan 5 nights $1,400 to $2,200 $14,000 to $22,000
Brazil 5 to 6 nights $1,500 to $2,500 $15,000 to $25,000
Marbella, Spain 4 to 5 nights $1,800 to $3,000 $18,000 to $30,000
Albania & Montenegro 7 nights $1,600 to $2,500 $16,000 to $25,000
Qatar 4 nights $1,600 to $2,700 $16,000 to $27,000

These are not quotations. The final cost will depend on season, hotel level, villa size, exchange rates, activities, birthday production and how many friends suddenly decide they deserve their own room. That last one can change the entire budget.

Before You Choose the Destination

A beautiful location is not enough. Can your guests realistically obtain the visa? Can they afford the flight? Does the destination work for the month of your birthday? Can the group move around easily? Is there enough to enjoy beyond the birthday dinner?

Most importantly, decide who the birthday is actually for. Sometimes we create celebrations around what looks impressive to other people. A milestone birthday should reflect the celebrant. Not Instagram, not family pressure, not what somebody else did last year.

Loving Itohan

Dear Ajayi

item.content:encoded:
Khaby Lame and Boubou Niang take the stage with a young participant at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games opening ceremony.

If you have been keeping an eye on sports and global pop culture, history was made over the weekend in West Africa. Senegal officially kicked off the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games with a spectacular opening ceremony at the 55,000-capacity Stade Abdoulaye Wade in Diamniadio, marking the first time an Olympic event has ever taken place on African soil.

Running through to 13 November, the Games are bringing together over 2,600 young athletes aged 14 to 17, competing across 25 sports and 153 medal events. The action spans three vibrant hubs: the historic capital city of Dakar, the modern satellite city of Diamniadio, and the coastal resort area of Saly.

Host nation Senegal enters the arena during the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games Parade of Nations.

Under the official motto “Africa welcomes, Dakar celebrates”, the opening ceremony turned into a celebration of music, dance, visual arts, and storytelling. Beyond the parade of nations, the night showcased iconic West African talent. Senegalese music legend Baaba Maal led a massive musical tribute alongside Kiné Lam and hip-hop outfit Daara J Family, while Gambian kora virtuoso Sona Jobarteh and social media star Khaby Lame made featured appearances.

Massamba Gueye performs during a cultural heritage sequence at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games opening ceremony.

Nigeria also took centre stage during the ceremony, with spoken word poet Ibukunoluwa Aramide Ajagbe, popularly known as Ibquake, delivering a live performance surrounded by dancers against a backdrop of stadium lights.

Ibquake performing live at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games opening ceremony.

The Games feature an exciting, youth-focused sports lineup including 3×3 basketball, futsal, beach volleyball, rugby sevens, breakdancing, street skateboarding, wushu, beach wrestling, table tennis, and archery. Over 200 National Olympic Committees are participating—with strong contingents representing African nations like host nation Senegal, Nigeria,South Africa, Kenya, and Algeria, alongside global delegations including Great Britain, Australia, Germany, Argentina, South Korea, and the United States.

With two full weeks of sporting events, cultural showcases, and youth competition ahead, Senegal has set the tone for a historic milestone in African sports and lifestyle history.

Following the fall of military ruler Lagata in Saworoide, the people of Jogbo hope for a new era of peace and prosperity. But the corrupt chiefs have other plans. Adebosipo, however, refuses to play along. Determined to protect the people of Jogbo, he demands accountability from the chiefs, setting off a fierce struggle over power, corruption and the future of the kingdom.

The conflict reaches a defining moment during a public traditional oath-taking ceremony before the sacred Agogo Èèwò, or Gong of Taboo. Under the custom, anyone who has stolen from the land must confess before the gong sounds seven times, or face the consequences.

Written by Professor Akinwunmi Isola and directed by Tunde Kelani, Agogo Èèwò remains a pointed examination of corruption, leadership and traditional systems of accountability. More than two decades after its original release, the film’s return in a remastered version gives audiences another opportunity to revisit the story and its enduring questions about those entrusted with power.

Senegal came alive yesterday at the opening ceremony of the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, with a vibrant celebration of culture, history and African creativity. She imagined her daughter one day asking when the Olympics first came to Africa, and how she would be able to tell her she was there. item.content:encoded:
ONGA, the seasoning brand from Promasidor Nigeria, marked World Food Day with its three-day Cook Your Way With ONGA activation, bringing shoppers together to explore Nigeria’s diverse food cultures and celebrate the individual touches that make every meal their own.

Rooted in ONGA’s Taste of Home platform, the campaign recognizes that home is not defined by one recipe or a single way of cooking. It is found in the meals people prepare their own unique way and share with loved ones, and in the everyday food experiences that bring comfort and connection. Through the campaign, ONGA is celebrating how people cook their food, not just what they cook, while highlighting its improved ONGA Chicken and Beef seasoning cubes as ingredients that make those meals enjoyable.

The activation kicked off on World Food Day, Friday, October 16, and was executed through Sunday, October 18, 2026, at Jendol Ikorodu, Akasolori, on Friday; Ikeja City Mall on Saturday; and Jendol Ibeju-Lekki on Sunday. Across the three locations, shoppers explored the food cultures of Nigeria’s six regions through regional food sampling, interactive games, and culinary challenges

At the ONGA Home booth, consumers experienced the taste of different homes such as Native Rice of the South-South region, Suya & Masa of the North-West region, Abacha of the South-East region, Dan Wake of the North-East region, Ofada & Ayamase of the South-West region, Jollof rice of the North-Central region, and took part in the “Cook Your Way With Onga” plate building game, which challenged them to match ingredients to a Nigerian dish against the clock.

Shoppers also shared stories about what makes their food uniquely theirs, while showing off their culinary skills through a cooking competition, and had opportunities to win rewards through the several interactive experiences at the event. 

Speaking on the campaign, Omotayo Olaobaju, Category Manager, Culinary at Promasidor Nigeria, stated:

“World Food Day Cook Your Way with Onga campaign was a fantastic platform to engage directly with our consumers online and offline. Onga believes that cooking is personal, and there is no standard recipe for great-tasting meals. Our role as a culinary partner is to inspire cooking confidence in every home ensuring that whichever recipe you choose, the improved Onga Beef or Chicken cube delivers guaranteed richness and taste

She also highlighted the ongoing digital challenge as another way for consumers to participate beyond the physical activations. 

The celebration continues online, where consumers can take part in the Cook Your Way with Onga digital challenge for a chance to win prizes including a kitchen makeover, an iPhone 18 Pro, a fridge and other rewards by sharing their unique ways of cooking their favourite meals on www.ongatasteofhome.com. Consumers can follow ONGA Nigeria on Instagram, Facebook, YouTube and TikTok for campaign updates and details on how to enter.

Through ‘Cook Your Way With ONGA’, the brand is bringing its ‘Taste of Home’ platform to life by celebrating the people, regional traditions and personal touches behind the meals that make home feel like home.

item.content:encoded:
L-R: Georgia Mobsby, Senior Manager – Sales Excellence; Anthony Uphill, Vice President Sales; Dave Geer, Chief Commercial Officer; Yann Stirton, Country Manager – West Africa; and Liezl Gericke, Head of International, all of Virgin Atlantic, at an awards evening in Lagos celebrating the airline’s 25 years of operations in Nigeria on 22nd October 2026.

British international airline Virgin Atlantic marks 25 years of operations in Nigeria with a special awards evening in Lagos, recognising the travel partners whose contributions have helped sustain and grow the airline’s presence in the country over the past quarter of a century.

Held at The George Lagos Hotel on Thursday, 22 October, the event brought together Virgin Atlantic executives, travel industry partners and other stakeholders to commemorate a journey that began in July 2001, when the airline launched its Lagos service with four weekly flights operated by a Boeing 747.

Speaking at the celebration, Virgin Atlantic’s Chief Commercial Officer, Dave Geer,
described Nigeria as one of the airline’s most important and established markets within its international network, paying tribute to the travel partners, customers, employees and operational partners who have contributed to its success.

“Technology will never replace relationships. The trust, local knowledge, and customer understanding represented in this room remain fundamental to our success,” Geer said. 

He also emphasized the importance of building sustainable partnerships, strengthening customer relationships and ensuring that the airline’s investments continue to support long-term commercial growth.

Virgin Atlantic’s Country Manager – West Africa, Yann Stirton, acknowledged the resilience of Nigerian travel partners, particularly through periods of economic uncertainty, currency volatility and restrictions on ticket inventory.

Highlighting a significant shift in the airline’s commercial performance, Stirton revealed that ticket sales in Nigeria now generate more revenue for the Lagos route than sales in any other market, including the United Kingdom.

“When I arrived in Lagos in September 2023, most of the revenue on this route was sold in the UK. Today, more revenue on this route is sold here in Nigeria than anywhere else in the world,” he said.

“That didn’t happen by accident. It happened because of the people in this room,” he added.

Stirton thanked travel partners for their continued support through challenging market conditions and expressed confidence in building on the relationship in the years ahead.

Virgin Atlantic executives and award recipients at a special awards evening held in Lagos on 22nd October 2026 to celebrate the airline’s 25 years of operations in Nigeria and recognise the outstanding contributions of its travel partners.

A major highlight of the evening was the presentation of awards recognizing outstanding contributions across commercial performance, innovation, growth, customer advocacy and partnership.

Among the recipients were ALML Travels and Tours, which received the High-Value Partner of the Year award; Wakanow.com, recognized for Digital Innovation and also named Agent of the Year – Retail; and Touchdown Travels, which received the Best Performing – TMC award in the travel management company category.

Other award recipients included 247 Travels, recognized as Best Performing – Retail;
Cinderella Travels, which received the Best Revenue Growth award; and FCM Travels and Ajala Travels, both recipients of the Rising Partner award.

The celebration also acknowledged the longstanding contribution of ALML, whose local expertise, operational support and relationships have played an important role in Virgin Atlantic’s Nigerian operations over the years.

Looking ahead, Geer reaffirmed Virgin Atlantic’s commitment to improving the customer experience through continued investment in its fleet, premium cabins and onboard connectivity.

The airline’s $17 billion fleet transformation programme will see Virgin Atlantic operate a fleet of 45 next-generation aircraft by 2028, alongside planned cabin upgrades to its Boeing 787-9 fleet and the introduction of additional Airbus A330neo aircraft. The carrier is also expanding free, high-speed Starlink Wi-Fi across its fleet, with fleet-wide coverage planned for 2027.

As Virgin Atlantic enters its next chapter in Nigeria, the airline remains focused on
deepening its relationships with travel partners, strengthening its commercial position and delivering an even better experience for customers.

You come for the collections, take notes on the street style, and leave with a camera roll full of inspiration. That is part of the thrill of Heineken Lagos Fashion Week, there is always something exciting that makes you stop and think, “I would never have thought of that.”

Rooted in cities and the cultures that shape them, Heineken finds inspiration in the people, creativity and experiences that give each city its character. This year, through City of Cities: Where Taste Rules, the brand celebrates Lagos’ distinctive energy with experiences spanning the Heineken Runway showcase, Heineken Lounge, the Nigerian debut of Heineken Studio and the Heineken After Party.

Curious? Here are five reasons to make room for Heineken in your Fashion Week plans:

  1. A Celebration of Fashion and Creative Expression

Ever wondered what happens when different styles, ideas and creative perspectives come together? Here is your chance to find out.

Last year, the City of Cities showcase featured a 46-piece collection curated by Omoyemi Akerele, bringing together designers including Atafo, Nkwo, Orange Culture, Dimeji Ilori and Eki Kere. From raffia and sequins to intricate hand-beaded details, the collection reflected the breadth of talent and craftsmanship within African fashion. 

In 2026, Heineken continues to celebrate the creative expressions that shape Lagos’ identity, building on its connection to cities and the cultures that make them unique through City of Cities: Where Taste Rules.

  1. Discover a New Expression of Taste at Heineken Studio

Fashion Week is a place for discovering what is next, and this year, Heineken is bringing that spirit of exploration to taste and socializing.

Last year, the Heineken District served as the week’s fashion-focused experience zone, hosting live recordings of fan-favourite podcasts from Tea with Tay to Off Air with Gbemi & Toolz and Toke Moments. Guest speakers and the hosts unpacked everything from sustainability to the evolution of style in Nigeria. Alongside it, the Drip’o’meter put a curated spotlight on the week’s most fashion-forward attendees. 

This year, Heineken is taking that spirit of exploration even further. Making its Nigerian debut, Heineken Studio will offer guests a closer look at the brand’s playground of innovation, exploring new ways to brew, serve and experience lager. It is one of the ways Heineken is bringing its innovation to life, inviting guests to discover what happens when brewing expertise meets a willingness to try something different.

  1. Connect with the People Shaping Lagos Culture

item.content:encoded:
Vitafoam Nigeria, one of the country’s leading mattress brands, recently announced the launch of the Vitafoam Luxury Collection, a new flagship range of premium mattresses designed to make purposeful and intentional rest an everyday standard for Nigeria’s discerning households who value productivity after every sleep.

These products are centred around two product series; is is anchored by two hero product series. First are the Vita Luxe premium comfort mattress and the Vita Helix hybrid foam-and-spring mattress. They are standard mattresses designed to bring the best of mattress technology to Nigerian homes. Vitafoam also introduced the Mattress- in-a-Box series, two products, Vita Restora and Vita Compresso, as well as VitaCool Plus pillow,  which brings the best of global engineering technology into the Nigerian market – the only company currently manufacturing this in the country. The series positioning: Rest Well. Live Fully is a significant shift in how ambitious Nigerians define success.

While many are proud to show stress and sleeplessness as a badge, we know the real measure of a life well lived is not only how hard one works, but how fully we show up, for family, for business, for milestones, for the moments that matter. The Vitafoam Luxury Collection positions rest not as slacking or indulgence, but as the foundation that makes everything else possible. 

The launch of the Vitafoam Mattress-in-a-box technology quietly changes the conversation in how mattresses are used, seen, moved, and set up in Nigeria. This is not imported but developed and produced within its factory and validated by its technical experts. This technology allows you order or pick up the product and transport with ease without the of moving it, fitting it through doors and taking it upstairs. The convenience factor is a game changer as it makes it now easy to gift people during weddings, birthdays and other traditional and cultural celebrations.  So easy it can be ordered via the Vitafoam website and delivered to yourself or the potential user. 

This luxury collection shows how seriously Vitafoam takes its category leadership as an opportunity to shape conversation around sleep, rest, and recovery, as well as how the evolving technology now makes it easy to move mattresses. 

Here are 10 things you need to know about the Luxury Collection and mattress-in-a-box technology.

01   It’s a whole new premium range, not a single product

The Vitafoam Luxury Collection presents a complete range of premium mattresses, not one new model. It is the brand’s most ambitious push into premium sleep in years, and a clear signal that ‘everyday luxury’ is no longer reserved for imported names.

02   Two flagships lead it: Vita Luxe and Vita Helix

Vita Luxe is the top of the range, deep, cradling premium comfort that gives an ordinary night the feel of a five-star hotel. Vita Helix is the premium hybrid: foam layers over a responsive spring system, engineered for support that lasts. Together, they anchor the collection.

03   Two signature products, a brand-new mattress-in-a-box range

Alongside the luxury line, Vitafoam has launched a mattress-in-a-box range: the premium hybrid Vita Restora and the convenient Vita Compresso. Both are engineered and compressed locally, so a full-size mattress can be delivered to your door in a package that can easily be transported. 


04   Yes, Mattress-in-a-box means a full mattress really comes rolled up in a box

It sounds like a trick, but it is simple engineering. A mattress is mostly air held inside foam. Vitafoam compresses that foam, vacuum-seals it, and rolls it tight enough to fit in a box one person can lift. You open it at home, and it expands back to a full-size bed within a few hours. No wrestling it onto a car roof, no law enforcement wahala.

05   You can order it online and have it delivered to your Door

Because the mattress-in-a-box ships like a normal parcel, you can buy it on the Vitafoam website and have it brought to you. For a mobile, urban, often-renting generation, the convenience of bringing it home without hassles is the real flex.

06   Vita Helix is built for support – especially couples

If your partner’s midnight turn always wakes you, Vita Helix is the answer. Its hybrid design includes motion isolation, which means movement on one side of the bed is absorbed rather than passed across. Two people, two sleep styles, one undisturbed night.

07   There’s a cooling pillow made for Nigerian heat

Completing the line-up is VitaCool Plus, a cooling pillow built for exactly the night you know too well; when the power goes, the fan stops, and the room turns to an oven. Heat-dissipating materials keep your head cool so the heat stops stealing your sleep.

08   It’s engineered and made in Nigeria

Every product in the range is designed and manufactured locally. That means no long import wait, steady availability, pricing in naira, and the backing of a Vitafoam warranty proof that ‘premium’ and ‘proudly Nigerian’ belong in the same sentence.

09   There’s a Vitafoam for every stage of life and every budget

While Vitafoam is Nigeria’s leading and trusted brand in mattress category, it’s brand of products covers every budget range. The Vitafoam Website contains lot of products within its standard range of products. The Luxury Collection also covers every stage of life. Vita Compresso suits the first apartment or a fresh start. Vita Restora fits the home you are building. Vita Helix is for couples and high performers. Vita Luxe is for when you have truly arrived. Wherever you are, whatever your sleeping style, there is a Vitafoam made for it.

10   The bigger idea: Vitafoam wants you to rest well so you can live fully

Beneath the products is a point of view. In a country that celebrates hustle, Vitafoam is making the case that you cannot live fully if you do not rest well. And that proper rest is not a reward for success, but the foundation of it. You deserve to have the flex of the fine art of living.

The Vitafoam Luxury Collection and Mattress-in-a-box range are available. You can either visit the comfort centres or order the Vita Cool Plus pillow, Vita Compresso, or Vita Restora via the Vitafoam website and have it delivered to you (in some selected states). 

Truly, Vitafoam defines The Fine Art of Living.

item.content:encoded:
The Africa Women Innovation and Entrepreneurship Forum (AWIEF) is pleased to announce its partnership with Open Society Foundations (OSF) for AWIEF 2026, taking place on 10 and 11 November 2026 at the Cape Town International Convention Centre (CTICC). The annual AWIEF Conference, currently in its twelfth edition, is a flagship convening of entrepreneurs, investors, corporates, government, and development partners from across Africa and beyond.

The partnership will take center stage during the opening plenary, Peace Dividends: Why Women-Led Enterprise Is a Security Strategy, Not Just an Economic One, exploring how women entrepreneurs contribute to economic stability, rebuild trust in communities affected by conflict, and help create the foundations for lasting peace.

Across fragile and post-conflict regions, from the Sahel to the Great Lakes and the Horn of Africa, women entrepreneurs play a vital role in restoring livelihoods and rebuilding local markets. Yet their contribution to peace building and security remains overlooked and unsung.

The plenary will examine how women-led businesses can strengthen community resilience, alongside the need for more effective access to capital, supportive policies and funding systems that empower their role in peace and development.

Opening Plenary: Peace Dividends

The discussion will be moderated by Idil Absiaye, Regional Head of Women, Peace and Security (WPS) Policy at UN Women, and feature:

  • Aimée Ongeso, Program Manager, Transformative Peace, Open Society Foundations.
  • Ibrahim Mulushewa Eshete, Co-Founder and Executive Director, Center for National and Regional Integration Studies (CeNRIS), Ethiopia.
  • Amb.  Ninikanwa O. Okey-Uche, Consul General, Consulate General of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, Johannesburg.
  • Yvette Mwanza, CEO of Kivu Mineral Resources and President of the North Kivu Chamber of Mines, Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

Bringing together perspectives from peace building, regional integration, diplomacy and business, the panel will explore what is working on the ground and what needs to change to better support women-led enterprises as contributors to peace and security.

Through this partnership, AWIEF and OSF will spotlight the connection between women’s economic empowerment, resilient communities and sustainable peace, reinforcing the importance of recognizing women entrepreneurs as not only drivers of economic growth, but also contributors to stability across Africa.

The opening plenary takes place on 10 November 2026 at the CTICC, Cape Town, as part of AWIEF 2026.

Registration and tickets for AWIEF 2026 Conference are available online at: https://www.awieforum.org/purchase-conference-tickets/#tickets

About AWIEF

AWIEF is a leading pan-African organisation advancing women’s economic inclusion through entrepreneurship, innovation and business leadership. Established since 2015, AWIEF has directly supported more than 6,500 female founders and entrepreneurs with enterprise development programs, training, and mentorship while facilitating access to finance, markets, and networks.

OSF supports individuals and organisations working to advance more just, inclusive and accountable societies.

item.content:encoded:
At the Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU), Ile-Ife 65th anniversary celebration, Dr. Tunji Olowolafe, Founder of the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation (TOF), called on Nigerian universities to open research to more people, test long-held beliefs with scientific rigour and carry discoveries out of the laboratory and into the economy.

Speaking on the theme, Promoting Research Excellence and Innovation in Postgraduate Studies: Charting the Future, Dr. Olowolafe reframed research as the disciplined habit of correcting a nation’s course based on evidence. He described the postgraduate college as the intellectual engine room of a nation, where society sends its sharpest minds to challenge conventional wisdom and demand honest, data-driven answers.

His first strategy called for opening the gates of research earlier, wider and more flexibly. He urged OAU to make its Staff Schools benchmarks for Africa, with science, technology and artificial intelligence at the core of the curriculum. He pointed to the Foundation’s Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial Community Secondary School in Are-Ekiti, which opened in September 2025 with 100 students and now has more than 170, alongside an ICT centre teaching artificial intelligence, coding, graphic design and Mandarin, with instructors teaching live from Beijing through a Starlink connection.

“The postgraduate researchers of 2040 are sitting in primary classrooms today,” he said.

He also questioned whether every road to postgraduate research must run through a four-year degree, inviting universities to recognize prior learning and demonstrated expertise without lowering standards. With only about one million of the two million UTME candidates admitted in 2025, he argued that flexible, digital study must become the standard model, since a digital campus needs no physical acreage. This builds on the Foundation’s Project Digi-Teach, which is training academic staff at Ekiti State University (EKSU) for digital proficiency.

His second strategy urged researchers to test what society believes. Rather than dismissing indigenous knowledge without investigation or defending it without validation, he called for rigorous testing, citing Chinese scientist Tu Youyou, whose study of a centuries-old herbal remedy produced the malaria treatment artemisinin and a Nobel Prize. He extended the same principle to national history, including sensitive chapters such as the Civil War.

“She neither rejected tradition nor accepted it. She tested it,” he said.

The third strategy focused on pushing research out of the laboratory and directly into the economy. Dr. Olowolafe advocated university promotion structures that reward patents, commercial products and solved industrial problems alongside traditional journal publications.

“Research is complete only when it leaves the laboratory and improves lives,” he said.

Pointing to OAU’s exceptional tech pedigree, including Flutterwave and Moniepoint founded by its graduates, he challenged the global alumni community to scale up their financial, institutional and mentorship support for research tenfold.

To support this vision, the Foundation will install a solar power system for the Postgraduate College, provide a virtual learning and oral defense facility and modernize the College Boardroom.

TOF will also fund pilot studies on a case-by-case basis and sponsor training in grant writing and donor compliance, working with OAU’s Central Office of Research and Advancement Office.

“Our ambition must go beyond providing infrastructure to building institutions that can generate knowledge and attract global research funding. By strengthening the capacity of our universities, we can expand opportunities for our people and position Nigeria to compete more effectively in the global knowledge economy,” he added.

Through these ideas and commitments, the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation continues to advance its broader ambition of strengthening the institutions, skills and opportunities that support Nigeria’s long-term development. Its work across education, digital learning and research capacity reflects a sustained commitment to equipping institutions and the next generation with the tools to compete and thrive in an increasingly knowledge-driven world.

item.content:encoded:
Visa, one of the world’s leaders in digital payments, applauds the launch of Google Pay by participating financial institutions in Nigeria, supported through Visa’s partnership with Google. Eligible Visa cardholders of participating financial institutions can now securely add their cards to Google Wallet and make fast, convenient, and secure payments across millions of contactless acceptance points and online merchants. 

The launch by participating financial institutions marks another significant milestone in Nigeria’s digital payments journey, providing consumers with a simple and secure way to pay using their Android devices. By adding their eligible Visa cards to Google Wallet, users can tap to pay in stores, make purchases online, and enjoy a seamless payment experience across Google’s ecosystem. 

Google Pay uses tokenization technology to help protect payment information. Instead of storing or sharing a customer’s card number during transactions, a unique digital token is used, providing an additional layer of security while maintaining a fast and convenient checkout experience. 

As consumer demand for digital-first payment experiences continues to grow, the partnership between Visa and Google, working alongside Nigerian financial institutions, aims to support contactless payment adoption and provide Nigerians with more ways to pay securely wherever Visa contactless payments are accepted. 

“At Visa, we are committed to advancing the future of payments by delivering innovative, secure, and seamless payment experiences for consumers across Nigeria and beyond.

Through our partnership with Google, we are pleased to support our financial institution partners as they bring Google Pay to their cardholders, combining the security of Visa’s global payment network with the convenience consumers increasingly expect in a digital-first world. Helping more people pay with confidence using their mobile devices supports digital commerce, financial inclusion, and the continued growth of Nigeria’s digital economy,” said Andrew Uaboi, Vice President and Cluster Head, Visa West Africa. 

“We are delighted to bring Google Wallet to Nigeria, a market at the forefront of financial innovation in Africa. Google Wallet makes everyday transactions faster and safer while removing the friction of carrying physical cards. By working alongside Nigeria’s leading financial institutions, we are expanding access to modern digital payment tools for millions of everyday consumers,” said Olumide Balogun, Country Director, Google West Africa

Visa (NYSE: V) is a world leader in digital payments, facilitating transactions between consumers, sellers, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories. The experience connected interior architecture with sourcing, craftsmanship and everyday life, demonstrating how collaboration transforms individual products into spaces with meaning.
For S.EA.CONSULTING, showing the world how we live begins with recognising the value of what we make, the stories we carry and the hands that bring our ideas to life.

item.content:encoded:
The Legacy Gala & Awards night: Fifty Years of Building More Than a Hotel. Fifty Years of Building a Nation’s Hospitality Identity.

2nd of October 2026 was written in the sands of time, because some hotels are built to accommodate history, others are built to make it.

For fifty years, Eko Hotels & Suites has done both. Beneath the lights of an extraordinary golden jubilee celebration, one of Africa’s most recognisable hospitality institutions made a statement that extended far beyond the walls of the magnificent Eko Convention Centre.

Africa does not lack the capacity to deliver world-class excellence. What it needs are more institutions courageous enough to demonstrate it.

The occasion was The Legacy Gala & Awards night, the grand celebration marking fifty years of Eko Hotels & Suites. An evening of African grandeur, international entertainment, cultural pride, distinguished personalities and extraordinary hospitality.

But to describe it simply as a glamorous anniversary celebration would be to misunderstand its significance.

This was not merely a party, It was fifty years of enterprise taking a bow, Fifty years of memories finding their voices, Fifty years of an institution reminding a continent that excellence is not foreign to Africa and for one unforgettable evening, history took attendance.

A Hotel Became Part of a Nation’s Story

There are buildings that occupy space, and there are institutions that occupy memory, Eko Hotels & Suites belongs to the latter.

Across five decades, its corridors have welcomed presidents and policymakers, entrepreneurs and entertainers, diplomats and dreamers, international visitors and generations of Nigerian families.

Within its halls, businesses have been negotiated, friendships formed, cultures celebrated, careers launched and milestones immortalized.

For many, Eko Hotels is where Lagos welcomes the world, for others, it is where the world first encounters the warmth, ambition, sophistication and extraordinary possibilities of Lagos.

Yet perhaps its greatest achievement is not simply that it has remained standing for fifty years. It is that it has remained RELEVANT. In a world where brands disappear as quickly as trends emerge, longevity is an achievement. But longevity accompanied by reinvention is leadership.

Eko Hotels has consistently demonstrated that hospitality must evolve beyond accommodation, It must become an experience, a cultural encounter, an economic opportunity, a reason to travel and  reason to return. Because the greatest hotels do not merely sell rooms. They give destinations a reputation worth travelling for.

The Night Africa Wore Her Crown

The Legacy Gala & Awards night brought together more than 1,000 distinguished guests, representing an extraordinary convergence of business, government, entertainment, culture and society.

Among the dignitaries were Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, Deputy Governor Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, prominent business leaders, industry executives, celebrities and long-standing friends of the institution.

It was a gathering that reflected not simply the prestige of a hotel, but the depth of relationships cultivated across generations.

The evening’s entertainment brought together internationally celebrated musician Wyclef Jean and Nigerian highlife sensation Flavour, creating a memorable meeting of African and Caribbean musical heritage.

Music, fashion, theatrical expression and celebration converged in a spectacle befitting the occasion. Yet, beyond the performances lay a more compelling message.

African creativity is not a decorative addition to hospitality. It is one of it’s greatest competitive advantages.

Africa’s music travels the world, African fashion influences global runways, African cuisine carries the memory of generations, African storytelling continues to captivate audiences far beyond our borders and, many started on Eko Hotels grounds.

The question is no longer whether Africa possesses what the world desires, the question is whether we are sufficiently intentional about converting these cultural assets into sustainable industries, jobs, investments and compelling destination experiences.

At The Gala, Eko Hotels offered its own answer. Africa need not borrow another continent’s identity to earn the world’s admiration. She need only invest boldly enough in her own.

There is, however, another story that deserves equal billing. It is the story of the people, not the famous faces photographed beneath the lights, not the glittering personalities whose arrival commands applause but the extraordinary men and women whose daily dedication has sustained Eko Hotels for half a century.

The housekeepers who prepare rooms with meticulous care, the waiters who understand that genuine service is an act of dignity, the engineers who keep an enormous hospitality operation functioning, the security personnel who protect its people and promises, the gardeners, technicians, stewards, reservation officers, accountants, sales professionals, event planners, administrative teams and countless others whose contributions rarely make newspaper headlines. These are the custodians of the brand. The quiet architects of its reputation and the human infrastructure behind its commercial success.

For fifty years, generations of employees have given their skills, energy, creativity and commitment to an institution that has become part of Nigeria’s hospitality heritage.

Their stories may not always appear in annual reports, but their fingerprints are everywhere.

A hotel may be built with concrete, steel and capital. But a legacy is built with people who choose, every day, to care. The Chairman, Christopher Chagoury boldly said in an interview.

Perhaps, this is one of the most important lessons of Eko Hotels at fifty: buildings can be replicated, interiors redesigned and technology acquired, but a culture of excellence must be nurtured and  that culture is ultimately human.

The Leadership understands the weight of the legacy.  Behind every enduring institution is a succession of decisions, investments, sacrifices and moments when leadership chooses long-term value over immediate convenience.

The golden jubilee provided an opportunity to recognize the vision and stewardship that have guided Eko Hotels through five decades.

Under the leadership of their Managing Director,  Ghassan Faddoul, General Manager  Danny Kioupouroglou and the wider executive management team, the institution continues to strengthen it’s position as a defining hospitality destination.

Their collective responsibility extends beyond protecting a celebrated past, to redesigning a future, our past will be proud of, long after we are gone.

It is to ensure that the institution remains competitive, innovative and relevant to future generations. The true measure of leadership, after all, is not simply what it achieves during its tenure, it is what remains valuable long after that tenure has ended.

Legacy is not the applause we receive while we are present. It is the relevance of what we build when we are no longer in the room. Fifty years of Eko Hotels is therefore not merely a tribute to endurance, it is a testament to institutional stewardship.

From Hospitality To Destination Economics 

Perhaps the most consequential chapter in Eko Hotels’ evolution is it’s expanding role in connecting hospitality with tourism, culture, entertainment and the creative economy.

Through initiatives such as Tropical Christmas Wonderland, Theatre @ Eko Hotels, Hakuna Matata Theme Park and other destination experiences, the institution has increasingly demonstrated how hospitality infrastructure can become a platform for cultural production and economic participation.

These initiatives represent a larger philosophy: a hotel should not wait for tourism demand to arrive. It can actively help create the reasons people travel.

A theatrical production creates opportunities for performers, designers, musicians, technicians and production professionals.

A festive destination experience stimulates spending across accommodation, food, transport, entertainment and retail.

A major international conference brings together airlines, logistics providers, service businesses and professionals. This is the multiplier effect of hospitality, it is also a reminder that tourism should not be treated as a decorative sector in national economic planning. It is an interconnected economic ecosystem.

Oil may have fed Nigeria’s treasury, but tourism possesses the potential to employ generations of her children.

The opportunity is enormous, provided the country develops the infrastructure, policies, investment climate and destination experiences necessary to realize it.

Eko Hotels’ evolution offers a practical illustration of what becomes possible when hospitality is approached as an economic engine rather than simply a property business.

The Africa Legacy Summit: When Celebration Became Conversation 

Importantly, Eko Hotels’ golden jubilee did not begin and end with a spectacular gala.

Earlier in May, the institution convened the Africa Legacy Summit, bringing together policymakers, scholars, diplomats, tourism professionals, business leaders, creatives and young Africans to explore the future of culture, hospitality, tourism and travel.

The summit asked a question of continental importance: How can Africa move beyond celebrating its potential to deliberately building the systems that convert that potential into prosperity?

Discussions examined cultural identity, tourism development, investment, sustainability, innovation, youth participation and the economic opportunities emerging across the continent.

It was an ambitious expression of the institution’s belief that celebrating fifty years should involve more than remembering the past, it should also contribute to shaping the future.

If the Africa Legacy Summit was the intellectual expression of Eko Hotels’ golden jubilee, The Legacy Ball was its cultural and emotional crescendo. One challenged Africa to think differently, the other demonstrated the extraordinary possibilities of African creativity and together, they communicated a powerful proposition:

Africa’s future will not be secured by repeatedly announcing her potential. It will be secured by institutions willing to organize that potential into measurable progress.

The Creative Intelligence Behind The Celebration 

For Dr. Iyadunni Gbadebo, Director of Sales and Marketing at Eko Hotels & Suites, the golden jubilee represented a significant opportunity to connect the institution’s history with a larger vision for African hospitality.

Over the years, her work in commercial strategy, destination experience development, theatre tourism, event curation and cultural marketing has contributed to initiatives that extend the hotel’s relevance beyond traditional accommodation.

Her approach reflects a growing recognition that hospitality brands must compete not only through their facilities, but through the experiences, stories and emotional connections they create.

The Legacy Ball formed part of this wider ambition to celebrate institutional achievement while presenting African creativity with confidence and sophistication.

As Gbadebo has consistently advocated, the continent must move from simply possessing exceptional cultural assets to developing commercially viable platforms that showcase them.

The distinction is critical as culture alone does not automatically create a tourism economy. It requires vision, investment, production, distribution, marketing and disciplined execution.

The world cannot buy an experience we have not had the courage to create. That philosophy has become increasingly visible in Eko Hotels’ evolving portfolio of cultural and experiential initiatives, and the next fifty years begins now.

As the celebrations drew to a close, the greater significance of the occasion became unmistakable. Eko Hotels & Suites had not simply commemorated fifty years of existence.

It had reaffirmed the importance of building institutions capable of transcending generations.

For Nigeria, the lesson is profound, national development is not achieved by government alone. It is strengthened by private enterprises that create employment, attract investment, nurture talent, maintain standards and build international confidence in their destinations.

Every enduring African institution becomes evidence that the continent is capable of building and sustaining excellence and every successful African experience challenges the outdated assumption that world-class quality must arrive from somewhere else.

Eko Hotels has spent fifty years welcoming the world to Africa. On one extraordinary night, it reminded the world why Africa deserves to be a destination, not merely a departure point.

The golden jubilee was magnificent, the performances were memorable, the personalities were distinguished but the true achievement was something much greater than spectacle. It was the celebration of an institution, the recognition of its people, the affirmation of it’s leadership and the demonstration of what African hospitality can become when ambition is matched with intention.

For fifty years, Eko Hotels has stood as one of Lagos’ defining hospitality landmarks. It’s next challenge is not simply to remain celebrated, it is to remain indispensable. Because the most powerful legacies are not monuments to yesterday, they are foundations upon which tomorrow is built.

Fifty years ago, a hotel opened its doors, five decades later, an institution stands before the world. If The Legacy Gala proved anything, it is that Africa does not need permission to be extraordinary, She needs more people willing to build the extraordinary  and sustain it.

EKO HOTELS & SUITES is 50!

The golden years are behind us. The golden possibilities are ahead.

item.title: Yinka Ogunbiyi Shows HaloBraid’s Automated Hair-Braiding Technology in New Demo
item.dc:creator: BellaNaija.com
item.description:
Nigerian-American engineer Yinka Ogunbiyi has shared a demo of HaloBraid, an automated salon device that helps hair braiders complete styles up to five times faster.

The post Yinka Ogunbiyi Shows HaloBraid’s Automated Hair-Braiding Technology in New Demo appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today!.
item.content:encoded:
Harvard graduate Yinka Ogunbiyi, creator of the automated HaloBraid device engineered to complete braids up to five times faster.

What if you could get your braids done in a fraction of the usual time and still leave the salon with the style you wanted? A new demonstration of HaloBraid, the automated braiding device created by Nigerian-American engineer and Harvard graduate Yinka Ogunbiyi, gives us a closer look at how that could work.

Designed to help professional hairdressers braid hair up to five times faster while reducing the physical strain that comes with hours of styling, HaloBraid is now being demonstrated in action. And the interesting part is that the machine doesn’t do everything. The stylist still plays an important role in the process.

Here’s how it works. The stylist sections the hair, applies the necessary products and starts the braid by hand before feeding it into the device. HaloBraid then handles the repetitive weaving along the length of the hair, while the stylist returns to finish and seal the ends. This means the machine takes care of a time-consuming part of the process, with the stylist still responsible for creating the final hairstyle.

For Yinka, the idea behind HaloBraid comes from a very personal experience. Sharing the story behind the invention, she said:

My braid story starts at age four, sitting between my mum’s legs as she braided my hair for the first time. Since then, I’ve spent thousands of hours getting my hair braided — and heard the same story from stylists and clients again and again: braiding is beautiful, but it takes too much time and too much strain.

As a biomechanical engineer, I knew there had to be a better way, so we built HaloBraid with stylists from the beginning, bringing together inventors, designers, and builders behind some of the world’s most loved hair and beauty products.

HaloBraid was built for my mum, my stylists, my aunties, and people around the world who know what it means to spend hours in the chair.

The company has also secured $7 million in seed funding, with the investment round led by Seven Seven Six, the venture capital firm founded by Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian, who is married to tennis champion Serena Williams.

With the newly shared demonstration, HaloBraid is showing how its technology works alongside professional stylists, combining hand-braiding techniques with automated weaving to reduce the time and physical effort involved in protective hairstyling.

item.title: How Can Africans Advance Cross-Country Equity and Opportunities Through AI?
item.dc:creator: BellaNaija Features
item.description:

item.content:encoded:
Photo source: Goalkeepers 2026 Report

For years, Africans have explored how to connect seamlessly without hurdles. As several opportunities are being explored through AI, Africans are also exploring whether AI can be used to advance cross-country opportunities and equity. If it can, what would it look like? What are the initial challenges that can hinder it from happening? What can governments and organisations do to enhance it?

Artificial intelligence is changing how people learn, work, build businesses and access information. For young Africans, what opportunities does it present to solve problems, develop new skills and participate in an economy that is becoming increasingly digital? How can those opportunities be available to everyone in the same way?

A young person with reliable internet access, a laptop and access to AI training has an advantage over someone who lacks these resources. The gap widens further when we consider young people across countries with different levels of digital infrastructure and investment. If AI is to improve the lives of African youth, access to its benefits must extend beyond the countries and communities already positioned to take advantage of it. African countries need to work together, share resources and invest in solutions that respond to the needs of their people.

Bill Gates in Rwanda. Photo by Jean Biziman for Gates Foundation

One area, and perhaps the most important area, where this cooperation matters is language. There are thousands of languages spoken in Africa. But much of the technology used to develop AI relies on data in widely spoken languages (in many cases in Africa, English and French), leaving many African languages underrepresented. This limits who can use these tools and how useful they can be. For a young person who speaks an African language but struggles with English or French, AI may not offer the same opportunities it offers someone who is fluent in these languages.

The Masakhane research community is working to address this problem by developing natural language processing technologies for African languages. The community consists of Africans representing different languages across Africa. It is an example of what can happen when African researchers collaborate to make technology more inclusive. Through initiatives such as the Masakhane AI Languages Hub, researchers can develop datasets across 40 African languages to support the creation of more useful AI tools.

In the 2026 Goalkeepers Report, Bill Gates said AI must be able to work in every language spoken to create significant equality.

Goalkeepers 2026 Report

African countries can build on this work by investing in shared language resources, supporting local researchers and making datasets available for responsible use. Instead of each country working independently on similar challenges, regional partnerships could help researchers share knowledge and develop tools that serve communities across borders. This could make it easier for young Africans to access educational resources, health information and other services in languages they understand.

AI can also help make opportunities available to people outside major cities. In agriculture, for example, PlantVillage Nuru uses a smartphone camera and AI to help farmers identify crop diseases. The application can work offline, making it useful in areas where internet connectivity is limited. Although the tool does not remove every challenge farmers face, it demonstrates how AI can make certain kinds of technical knowledge more accessible.

Solutions like this could benefit young farmers and agricultural entrepreneurs across Africa. Countries facing similar agricultural problems could collaborate to test, adapt and improve existing tools instead of developing separate solutions from the beginning. Universities, research institutions and governments could support these efforts by sharing expertise and investing in technologies that respond to local conditions.

African countries can work together to create more opportunities for young people to learn AI skills, participate in research, access mentorship and build businesses. Regional programmes could connect students with employers and investors across borders, allowing talent to find opportunities beyond national job markets. They could also help young people learn from one another and develop solutions that can be adapted to different African communities.

Bill Gates in Rwanda. Photo by Jean Biziman for Gates Foundation.

These efforts must be supported by investments in electricity, affordable internet, devices and digital education. Without these basics, AI training and other opportunities may continue to reach those who already have the most access. Governments and technology companies must also protect users’ data, address bias and ensure that the development of AI does not exclude women, people with disabilities or young people in rural communities.

The African Union’s Continental Artificial Intelligence Strategy, endorsed in 2024, provides a basis for countries to pursue a more coordinated approach to AI development. The challenge now is to translate that ambition into practical opportunities for young people.

Africa does not have to approach every AI challenge as a separate national problem. By sharing knowledge, supporting local innovation and opening more pathways to education and employment, countries can make their investments go further. Success should not be measured only by the number of AI tools developed or the amount of money invested in the technology. It should also be measured by whether a young person, regardless of where they live, has a fair chance to use AI to improve their life.

This will be part of the conversation centred around this year’s Goalkeepers 2026. After hosting engaging and immersive events in the Nordics and New York, Goalkeepers is coming to Dakar on October 29 for the event, “Equitable AI and the Future of African Youth.”

item.content:encoded:
Taiwo Awoniyi posing on the red carpet at the Best of Africa Awards 2026 in London.

Nigerian international striker Taiwo Awoniyi has picked up the prestigious ‘Beyond the Pitch’ Award at the 2026 Best of Africa Awards in London, marking a major moment of recognition for his work both on and off the football field.

Known for his clinical goalscoring ability and strength upfront, the Nottingham Forest and Super Eagles forward plays as a central striker at the highest level of European football. Beyond his professional career in the English Premier League, Taiwo has consistently directed his resources towards community development, healthcare support, and youth empowerment in Nigeria—most notably through his funding and sponsorship of the Kwara Kiddies League, an initiative providing structured grassroots football opportunities for young talents in Kwara State.

The Best of Africa Awards, held annually in London, celebrate the outstanding contributions of African figures and individuals of African heritage across sports, entertainment, and social impact. Supported by the Professional Footballers’ Association (PFA), the ‘Beyond the Pitch’ accolade specifically highlights athletes who use their global platform to drive tangible social change and uplift their home communities.

Taking to Instagram to reflect on the honour, Taiwo shared a message with his followers:

Life can give you so much, but what truly matters is what you choose to do with what you’ve been given. Grateful to receive the PFA Beyond the Pitch Award at the Best of Africa Awards 2026.

His philanthropic commitments include fully funding the annual Kwara Kiddies League tournament, providing kits, equipment, and cash prizes for grassroots teams across Ilorin and surrounding areas to help young footballers build sustainable career pathways.

item.content:encoded:
Heineken returns to Lagos Fashion Week from October 29 to 31, 2026, continuing a decade-long partnership that has evolved beyond sponsorship into a platform for creative collaboration, cultural expression and shared experiences. Through City of Cities: Where Taste Rules, Heineken will celebrate the people, cultures and creative expressions shaping Lagos, bringing its presence to life across the Heineken Lounge, Heineken Runway Showcase, Heineken Studio and the After Party.

First introduced in Lagos in 2025, City of Cities: Where Taste Rules celebrates the diversity that defines the city, where different cultures, styles, communities and perspectives converge. From fashion and music to food, art and social experiences, Lagos draws its character from the people and influences that shape it. For Heineken, this reflects the many ways taste is expressed, experienced and shared.

Over the past decade, Heineken’s partnership with Lagos Fashion Week has evolved through initiatives that explore the relationship between fashion, craftsmanship and taste. From the sustainable fashion focus of Woven Threads in 2022 and the Dyelab collaboration in 2023 to the H45 Collection in 2024 and the introduction of City of Cities: Where Taste Rules in 2025, each chapter has offered a distinct expression of the partnership. In 2026, Heineken continues this legacy, creating new opportunities to connect with the people, ideas and experiences shaping contemporary Nigerian fashion and culture.

This year’s Heineken Lagos Fashion Week theme, CRAFTED, provides a natural context for this next chapter, celebrating intentionality, artistry, craftsmanship and more considered approaches to fashion and sustainability. Reflecting this spirit, Heineken will bring its presence to life across the week through the Heineken Lounge, the Cruise Collection runway, Heineken Studio and the Heineken Studio After Party, creating experiences that extend beyond the runway.

Making its Nigerian debut, Heineken Studio introduces a new dimension to the brand’s exploration of taste and innovation. Described as Heineken’s Playground of Innovation, Studio explores new ways to serve and experience lager through experimentation, brewer expertise and discovery. Experiences such as Foam Infusions will invite guests to discover unexpected flavour combinations, bringing a fresh perspective to taste within the wider Heineken Lagos Fashion Week experience.

Speaking on the experience, Sandra Amachree, Head of Marketing and Communications at Nigerian Breweries, said: “For a decade, our partnership with Heineken Lagos Fashion Week has been a meaningful expression of Heineken’s connection to fashion, creativity and culture. This year, with the continuation of City of Cities: Where Taste Rules, we are building on that legacy with experiences that celebrate the people, ideas and creative energy that make Lagos unique. The Nigerian debut of Heineken Studio brings a new dimension to this experience, inviting guests to discover new expressions of taste and innovation while connecting through a shared appreciation for fashion and culture. We look forward to another exciting chapter of this partnership and to celebrating the creativity that continues to shape Lagos.”

Through City of Cities: Where Taste Rules, Heineken continues to celebrate Lagos as a city shaped by diverse tastes, cultures and creative expressions. At Heineken Lagos Fashion Week 2026, the brand looks forward to another chapter of its partnership, bringing people together through fashion, taste and socialising.
